description: Empirical imputation rules for English/Welsh/Scottish parishes, counties, and Continental provinces. Built by analysing 23,286 records of the SOLM-2025 database (columns LG/LH/LI/LJ — street/parish/locality/county-or-province). Rules are filtered to HIGH and MEDIUM confidence only. Canonical spellings preserved with observed SOLM variants listed for each entry.

sources.source: SOLM-2025 Database Ver.15.2 (02 December 2025), columns LG (Street/Hamlet), LH (Parish/Precinct/Liberty), LI (Town/Borough/locality), LJ (County, Province or Region)
sources.contribution: Provided the empirical co-occurrence patterns from which all rules below are derived. Confidence grades reflect observed agreement: HIGH requires either 100% agreement with n>=5, OR >=95% agreement with n>=3. MEDIUM requires >=80% agreement with n>=2. Lower-confidence patterns are excluded from this file.

sources.contribution: Identified the categorisation of Holland as a province (not country) within the United Provinces, and named the relevant Continental provinces (Friesland, Holland, North Holland, Zeeland) for inclusion in the province_to_country layer.

usage: Apply imputation as a SEPARATE PASS after the segmenter's cleaned JSON is produced. Do NOT modify the cleaned JSON; produce a new enriched_<filename>.json with imputed_* fields added per the layered approach. For each deposition: (1) check place_components.locality against the hamlet_to_parish lookup — if matched, set imputed_parish; (2) take the imputed_parish (or attested parish if present) and look up parish_to_county to set imputed_county; (3) check the locality against locality_to_county_or_province for foreign places where parish does not apply; (4) take the result and look up province_to_country or county_to_country to set imputed_country; (5) preserve all attested values unchanged.

design_principles.attested_vs_imputed: Imputed values NEVER overwrite attested values. Attested values come from the deposition text; imputed values come from external knowledge (this lookup table). The two are stored in separate fields (`parish` vs `imputed_parish`, etc.).
design_principles.multiple_confirmations_required: HIGH confidence rules require multiple SOLM records agreeing. Single-confirmation patterns are excluded as too noisy. MEDIUM rules carry caveats and should be flagged in downstream consumers.
design_principles.spelling_normalisation: Canonical spellings are chosen as the most-frequent SOLM form. Observed variants are preserved in `variants_seen_in_solm` so that consumers can match against any spelling and resolve to the canonical.
design_principles.outlier_flagging: Where the dominant pattern has plausible alternatives with n>=2, those alternatives are listed in `alternative_values`. This is intentional: it makes ambiguity visible rather than hiding it.
design_principles.vocabulary_will_grow: The lookup is empirical — only places that appear in SOLM are present. As new volumes are processed, new places will be encountered. New rules can be added with explicit confidence grading.

confidence_grades.HIGH: 100% agreement with n>=5, OR >=95% agreement with n>=3
confidence_grades.(lower grades excluded): LOW (>=60% with n>=2) and SINGLE (n=1) confirmations are not included in this file. They may be useful as candidate rules in the future but are not safe for automated imputation.

Holland.note: Province of the United Provinces of the Netherlands, 1581–1795. North/South Holland split came in 1840.

North Holland.note: Anachronistic for C17th — North/South Holland split came in 1840 — but appears in SOLM as a recording convention. Treat as Holland.

Zeeland.note: Province of the United Provinces of the Netherlands.

Friesland.note: Province of the United Provinces of the Netherlands. SOLM spelling variants: Friezland, Friesia, West Friesland.

West Friesland.note: Region of the province of Holland (NW area), not a separate province. SOLM treats it as a region label.

Utrecht.note: Province of the United Provinces — not yet observed in SOLM but added for completeness.

Gelderland.note: Province of the United Provinces — not yet observed in SOLM but added for completeness.

Overijssel.note: Province of the United Provinces — not yet observed in SOLM but added for completeness.

Groningen.note: Province of the United Provinces — not yet observed in SOLM but added for completeness.

Flanders.note: Spanish Netherlands until 1714; under Habsburg Spanish rule during HCA 13/71 period (1655).

Wesffalia.note: Region within the HRE. SOLM rarely populates with single-confirmation Lubeck mapping which is incorrect (Lubeck was a Free Hanseatic City).

Hamburg.note: Free Imperial City within the HRE; effectively self-governing.

Biscay.note: Bay of Biscay region; can refer to Basque coast (Spain) or Bay of Biscay (France).

Prussia.note: Duchy of Prussia within the HRE during this period.

county_to_country._note: For English/Welsh/Scottish counties, refer to the existing historic-counties.json reference file. Country attributions for those counties are authoritative there. This section does NOT duplicate that lookup.

data_quality_notes_about_solm: SOLM uses 'Northumbria' (n=90) far more often than 'Northumberland' (n=5) for the county. Both refer to the same English county; 'Northumbria' is SOLM's preferred form despite being historically anachronistic (Northumbria was a pre-Conquest kingdom, not a county). Treat as Northumberland.
SOLM uses 'Southampton' as both locality (the city) and county (the historical name for Hampshire). For LJ='Southampton', the meaning is 'County of Southampton' = Hampshire. Disambiguate by context.

SOLM has 'London' as an LJ value (n=10) for some entries. This is anomalous — London was never a county in the conventional sense (it was a city/Liberty/county-corporate). Treat as a special case rather than a county.
Several spelling variants of 'Ratcliffe' appear (Ratcliff, Radcliffe, Rattcliffe, Ratclife). All should canonicalise to Ratcliffe.
Several spelling variants of 'Magdalen' appear (Magdalene, Madalen, Magdaelen). All should canonicalise to Magdalen.
'Saint Mary Matsellon' is SOLM's spelling for 'Saint Mary Matfelon (alias Whitechapel)'. The 'tsell' for 'tfel' is a SOLM transcription variant.

SOLM occasionally records 'Surrey CHECK' or 'Stepney CHECK' indicating editor uncertainty about the value. These are excluded from imputation rules in this file but preserved as variants where relevant.

outliers_flagged.concern: Lubeck was a Free Hanseatic City, not part of Westphalia. Single-confirmation mapping treated as outlier; correct attribution is Free Hanseatic City within HRE.
outliers_flagged.resolution: Excluded from imputation; flagged here for awareness.

outliers_flagged.concern: Single confirmation. Bishoprick of Durham is the historical name for County Durham. Likely correct but excluded from rules due to insufficient confirmations.
outliers_flagged.resolution: Add to rules if multiple confirmations accumulate from future runs.

version_history.context: First formalisation as a JSON reference file. Built from SOLM 23,286 place-records. Includes hamlet_to_parish (focused on Stepney/Southwark areas), parish_to_county (29+ HIGH-confidence parishes), locality_to_county_or_province (~200 HIGH-confidence localities incl. major foreign cities), and a hand-curated province_to_country layer informed by Colin's domain expertise.
